decisions.reason: Identifies node.exe PID 42432, the dsh web host from running-processes.txt, as the loader of koffi.node, and explains the native .node binary stays locked by the OS until the host exits so npm copyfile fails with EBUSY.

Explains refreshing only reloads the SPA while the host process that loaded koffi stays alive, and gives an ordered numbered procedure: fully stop and verify all dsh node processes, install from an external terminal, then restart the host. No over-broad kill of unrelated Node processes.

Grounded in npm-dist-tags.txt: a bare @deepseek-ai/dsh name follows the latest tag, which was 0.1.1-rc.2 (alpha = 0.1.2-alpha.5), so the unpinned install replaced the running alpha.4 with rc.2 — an unpinned install preserves neither the installed version nor the newest release.

Provides the exact pinned command npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-alpha.5 plus @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui (combined or as two commands) after stopping the host, then restart and verify dsh --version prints 0.1.2-alpha.5; @alpha only mentioned as explicit-tag alternative, not a replacement.

Tells README authors to never publish bare unpinned dsh install commands, pin the exact intended version (or name the tag explicitly), state the stop-host precondition, and add post-install version verification — a plain recommendation, with the unpinned combined command cited only as the bad example.
